admin.areaExplains: An area is where work is filed. Declaring one here is what stops two spellings of the same name becoming two areas that never meet.
admin.areaFolds: Becomes a lowercase identifier, without accents and with hyphens in place of spaces.
admin.areaHint: An area is where work is filed: an agent belongs to one, a ceiling governs one, a policy reaches a set of them and a grant is held in one. Undeclared, every screen invents its own from whatever exists.
admin.ceilingApplies: Applies from the next run; one already stopped resumes when there is room.
admin.ceilingsInherit: Ceilings inherit downwards and never widen: an area cannot raise what its company allows. Reaching one pauses the run and it continues from where it stopped, rather than ending.
admin.effectDestructive: Erases or replaces in a way that is hard to undo.
admin.eventsHint: Every configuration change appears here with who made it and when: classifying a tool, registering a provider, removing a server.
admin.inCurrency: In the installation's currency. Leave empty not to cap by amount.
admin.name: Name
admin.noCeilingHint: With no scope ceiling, the only limit is what each agent specification sets per run — nobody can cap an area. Reaching a ceiling pauses the run and it continues later.
admin.readMarksRun: A read marks the run. A write after that stops for a person to decide.
admin.recordedInTrail: Recorded in your name in the administrative trail. Correcting it later creates a new record; no record is erased.
admin.removeCeiling: Runs in that scope become bounded only by each agent's per-run ceiling. It is recorded in the trail.
admin.sayCompany: Say which company the area belongs to.
admin.subtitle: What the platform talks to, what each tool does to the world, and who changed what.
admin.whatItDoes: What this tool does to the world
admin.withdrawArea: It stops being offered for new work. The agents, ceilings and policies already filed under it keep pointing at it and keep applying — withdrawing an area and rewriting the past are different acts.

agents.areaIsUnit: The area is the unit of cost and of policy.
agents.budgetNeeded: A run needs at least a cost or a step ceiling: it is what makes it finite, and ending is structural here, never something asked for in the prompt.
agents.callerAlsoNeeds: The caller also has to send an
agents.configureNow: Configure the calling system now. This is the only time it is shown — the platform keeps only its digest.
agents.emptyCatalogue: No tool in the catalogue. An MCP server has to be connected before an agent can do anything at all.
agents.emptyHint: Agents appear here when a worker publishes the definitions it loaded. Each publication creates a new version; the previous one stays readable.
agents.idempotencyExplains: The caller also has to send an Idempotency-Key unique per delivery, repeating the same value on every retry of that delivery. Without it, a redelivery opens a second run.
agents.instructionsLength: {{count}} characters. It is the text the published version carries, and what an auditor will read to understand a run two years from now.
agents.instructionsPlaceholder: You handle tickets arriving at support@…
agents.keptOutsideTrail: Kept outside the trail, like all content: a ticket routinely carries personal data and the trail is held for years.
agents.neverRan: This agent has never run. Runs start from the command line while triggers do not exist.
agents.noMatch: No agent with that name, in that area and in that state.
agents.noTools: No tool. This agent cannot touch anything outside the model.
agents.noTriggers: Nothing. This agent only runs when somebody opens it here.
agents.notHereNotInvokable: What is not here cannot be invoked, whatever the instructions ask for.
agents.nothingChanged: Nothing changed. Publishing now would return the version that already exists: the version is the digest of the content, and the same text is the same version.
agents.pausedOnCreate: A new agent is created paused. Publishing writes the definition; starting is a separate decision, and all four ways of opening a run obey it.
agents.pausedStartWhenReady: The agent is paused. Start it when you want it to run.
agents.publishWritesVersion: Publishing writes a new version. Runs already made stay pinned to the version that ran in them.
agents.publishedWithout: This version was published with no instructions.
agents.rightColumnIsPolicy: The right-hand column is what the policy in force will do, not a setting on this agent. Changing it means editing the policy — which has an owner, a reason and a code that appears in the trail.
agents.riskNothing: Nothing. With no tools, this agent can only reason.
agents.rotateWarning: The current key stops working immediately. Every system configured with it will start receiving 401 until it is updated with the new one.
agents.runOpensOnPublished: The run opens on the version published now and is recorded in your name. A person still decides any action that requires approval.
agents.runsUnreadable: Could not read this agent's runs.
agents.subtitle: Every published version is immutable: the identifier is the digest of the content, so the text a run executed can always be read back.
agents.textAlreadyPublished: This text was already the published version.
agents.zeroIsNoCeiling: Zero means no ceiling, which is not the same as a ceiling of zero.

approvals.emptyHint: When an agent proposes an action that needs a human decision, it appears here with the reason and what the action does.
approvals.notePlaceholder: Stays in the trail alongside the decision
approvals.subtitle: Steps where an agent stopped because a person has to decide. The decision stays in the trail, with whoever made it.

audit.emptyHint: The Gate's decisions, the human approvals and every change anybody makes to the rules appear here — classifying a tool, configuring a provider, setting a ceiling.
audit.sealedEntries: <n>{{count}}</n> ledger entries, chained by hash — each one seals the one before it.
audit.subtitle: What the agents did and what people changed in the rules they run under. Both records are append-only; only one is chained.
audit.unsealedEntries: <n>{{count}}</n> from the administrative trail: append-only by grant, not chained.
audit.verifyIsPerRun: Verifying the chain is done per run, in that run's trail.

common.loadFailedHint: Check the connection to the server and try again.

cost.cacheShare: of what went into the model, at a fraction of the price
cost.emptyHint: Cost appears as soon as the first run finishes. If runs have already happened and the figure is zero, the model provider has no price table — the platform counts tokens and refuses to guess at money.
cost.noCapsHint: With no scope ceiling, the only limit is each agent's own per run. Configure one under Administration → Ceilings.
cost.noTokens: No token accounted for in the period.
cost.spentPerDay: Spent per day over the last 14 days
cost.subtitle: Every run has a known cost before anybody decides to scale it. The run is the accounting unit; agent, area and period are cuts of it.

gate.badArgs: The arguments do not match the tool's contract.
gate.duplicate: This call is already in the trail; repeating it would duplicate the effect.
gate.humanCleared: Cleared by a human decision recorded in this run.
gate.outOfPack: The tool is outside the run's capability pack.
gate.overCeiling: The call would exceed the run's ceiling.
gate.policyRequires: The installation's policy requires handling for that kind of effect.
gate.tainted: The arguments derive from untrusted data read at an earlier step.

integrations.credentialKept: One is already stored. Leave blank to keep it.
integrations.credentialSealed: The credential is sealed the moment it arrives and never comes back through this screen.
integrations.credentialVault: Sealed in the vault; not even this screen can read it back.
integrations.mcpExplains: An MCP server is what gives agents their tools. Everything it offers arrives as a read until somebody classifies it.
integrations.neverTried: No worker has tried to connect yet.
integrations.noProviderHint: With no provider no run advances: the agent has nothing to plan with.
integrations.noServerHint: An MCP server is what gives agents their tools. Until there is one, agents can only reason.
integrations.referencedBySpecs: It is what agent definitions reference.
integrations.removeProvider: Runs that depend on this provider stop advancing. It is recorded in the trail.
integrations.removeServer: Agents lose this server's tools at the next worker restart. It is recorded in the trail.
integrations.subtitle: Everything the agents reach outside this installation, and whether it is answering.

notFound.hint: The address matches no screen in the console. It may be an old link, or a screen nobody has built yet.
notFound.title: This screen does not exist

overview.noAgents: No agent published. A published definition appears here with the day's activity.
overview.noCeilingConfigured: No scope ceiling configured, so there is no denominator for a percentage. Spent today: {{spent}}.
overview.noDecisions: The Gate decided nothing today. No agent asked to run a tool in the period.
overview.noRunsToday: No run today. Agents are opened by a schedule, a webhook or an event.
overview.subtitle: How the day is going: how much ran, what the Gate decided and what it cost.

policies.codeAppears: The code appears in the trail and in the message shown to whoever is denied.
policies.editorSubtitle: A rule evaluated at every agent step: scope, condition, and what happens when it matches.
policies.emptyHint: With no rules written, the built-in default applies: a read passes, a write asks for human approval, and a destructive or financial effect is denied. A written policy tightens that default — or opens an exception with somebody's name on it.
policies.enforcingNextStep: Enforcing from the next agent step.
policies.monitoring: Monitoring, the rule is evaluated and recorded and stops nothing.
policies.mostRestrictiveWins: The order between policies does not change the outcome: the Gate returns the most restrictive decision among all that match. Deny beats escalate, which beats allow.
policies.noCondition: With no condition the rule covers everything its scope reaches.
policies.noneSelectedCoversAll: None selected covers all of them.
policies.nothingToSimulate: No decision recorded in the period, so there is nothing to simulate. That does not say the rule is harmless — it says there was nothing to compare against.
policies.onlyExceptionIsAllow: The only exception is an allow that matched: it is the one thing that loosens the built-in default, and that is what an exception is.
policies.reasonExplains: It appears in the trail and to whoever is stopped. It is the difference between “blocked by {{code}}” and knowing what to do about it.
policies.ruleEvaluated: The rule that will be evaluated
policies.scopeReach: What the rule reaches before any condition.
policies.simulationExplains: Runs this rule against decisions already recorded and shows what it would have done, before saving.
policies.subtitle: The rules the Gate evaluates at every agent step. A policy in monitor mode is evaluated, recorded, and changes nothing.
policies.unknownDecisions: <n>{{count}}</n> decisions could not be answered: this rule reads arguments, and refused calls never stored any. The number above is a floor, not a total.
policies.willApplyAfterReload: It applies at the next agent step once the workers reload the set.
policies.willBeMonitored: It will be evaluated at every step its scope covers, recorded in the trail, and will change no decision.

runs.argumentsGone: The arguments are no longer available. Retention erases the content; the trail keeps its digest.
runs.changedState: This run changed state in at least one system.
runs.contentGone: The content is no longer available. Retention erases it; the trail keeps its digest.
runs.emptyHint: Runs appear here as soon as an agent is opened by a schedule, a webhook or an event. Widen the period or clear the state filter.
runs.foldSummary: {{count}} routine steps · allowed reads, no state changed
runs.noMatchFor: No run or agent matching "{{query}}". The search respects the period and the state selected.
runs.noToolsCalled: No tool was called in this run.
runs.noWrites: No write was executed in this run.
runs.storyInsisted: the model insisted on a refused call and the run was interrupted
runs.subtitle: Every run is the unit of audit and of cost: what the agent proposed, what the Gate decided and what actually happened.
runs.taintedArguments: The arguments derive from data marked <l>{{labels}}</l> at an earlier step of this run.
runs.verifyExplains: Verifying recomputes the whole chain and says at which step it breaks.

session.noProvider: No identity provider is configured. Whoever administers this installation has to register one before anybody can sign in.
session.recordedAsClaimant: Recorded as whoever claimed the installation.
session.sayWhoYouAre: Say who you are, for the trail to record.
session.setupOnce: This happens only once. After it, access goes through the identity provider you configure.
session.tokenInLog: The token was printed to the server log at startup, and is good for 24 hours.
session.useOrgAccount: Use your organisation's account. The access you get comes from the groups it reports.
